_comment: darkmux profile registry — example. Three worker profiles in increasing capacity order (fast → balanced → deep), plus one hosted-endpoint example. A profile's `models[]` are WORKER models; the machine's standing utility/compactor model lives once in the top-level `internal.utility`. `n_ctx` is required for LOCAL models (it is the load parameter) and omitted for endpoint-bearing models. `darkmux init` fills the `<your-worker-model-id>` slots from a model you have downloaded; run `lms ls` to see them, and `darkmux config set role_profiles.<role> <profile>` to staff a mission seat. Profiles for the review mission's `reviewer` seat are in the guide, not here.

fast.description: Single-turn tasks. Slim worker — fastest dispatch, lowest RAM.

balanced.description: Mid-range tasks. Predictable behavior across mixed workloads; compaction runs on the machine's internal.utility model.

deep.description: Long agentic tasks. Maximum worker context for fewer compactions.

hosted-frontier.description: A hosted model instead of a local one — no n_ctx (the provider owns the context window). Add an `auth` block when your endpoint needs credentials; see the guide. Delete this profile if you only run local models.
